title: Graphutzing around with Solr
subtitle: Notes on querying graphs in Solr
date: 2022-08-03

Some practical exploration of graph operations in Solr.

Solr graph operations basically involve a breadth-first scan across documents connected by some property from a starting set of documents and optionally applying filters during the traversal or on the resulting set of documents.



Examples in these pages use a default Solr setup using Docker, configured to expose Solr on port `18983` using the following `docker-compose` file:

```{.yaml include=docker-compose.yml .numberLines}
```

Run the instance like `docker-compose up -d`. 

Test data:
```{.json include=test-data.json .numberLines .includeLink}
```



```{python}
import json
import graphutzing

docs = json.load(open('test-data.json', 'r'))
g = graphutzing.generateViz(docs)
g
```


```{python}
import igraph

g = igraph.Graph()
g.add_vertices(3)
g.add_edges([(0,1), (1,2)])
g.add_edges([(2, 0)])
g.add_vertices(3)
g.add_edges([(2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 5), (5, 3)])
print(g)
layout = g.layout("kk")
igraph.plot(g, layout=layout)
```
